title: LPFormer: An Adaptive Graph Transformer for Link Prediction

problem.claim: Link prediction requires identifying links that may form between nodes in graph-structured data.

gap.claim: Existing pairwise encodings use the same underlying factors for all links, limiting adaptation to links formed by different factors.

contributions.claim: LPFormer adaptively learns pairwise encodings for each candidate link.
LPFormer uses an attention module to model multiple link factors when learning pairwise encodings.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish LPFormer as a new method for addressing the limitations of existing pairwise encodings.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that LPFormer achieves state-of-the-art performance on numerous datasets while maintaining efficiency.
The authors report that the code is available on GitHub.

narrative_sequence.summary: Link prediction is a common graph-data task historically addressed with hand-crafted heuristics.
Recent methods combine MPNN outputs with pairwise encodings and have shown strong performance on multiple datasets.
Current pairwise encodings impose a common factorization bias across links, limiting classification of diverse links.
LPFormer addresses the limitation by adaptively learning link-specific pairwise encodings through attention over multiple factors.
The authors report state-of-the-art performance with efficiency and provide code.

source_observation.claim: Existing pairwise encodings may apply the same underlying factors to every link.

interpretation.claim: A shared representation can restrict a model when different instances depend on different explanatory factors.

application.claim: For heterogeneous pairwise prediction tasks, consider instance-adaptive representations that can model multiple factors.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when adaptive representations outperform shared encodings or what trade-offs they introduce.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, quantitative results, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not describe the attention architecture or training procedure in detail.
The abstract does not provide efficiency measurements or computational-resource requirements.
